raw_response:
I am 74 years old. I only have 2 mu, just a little patch. My wife and me, and my son when he comes home. I have grown cotton here for many years. Every year I do about the same, because what I do works well enough.

For seeds, I buy the kind from the dealer in town. Everyone buys this kind now — the kind that the bollworm does not eat so much. My neighbor Old Wang plants it, his cotton is good, so I plant it too. I buy maybe half a jin of seed for my 2 mu, the dealer tells me how much.

For fertilizer, before I plant, I spread 2 bags of the compound fertilizer — the one with three numbers on the bag — one bag each mu. That bag is 50 jin. Then when the cotton starts to flower, I put urea, maybe half a bag each mu, because that is when the plant needs strength to make bolls. If the leaves look yellow I put a little more. My neighbors all do like this. Too little and the bolls will be small, and I cannot afford a bad year on only 2 mu. Better to put a little extra than lose the harvest.

I plough the field in spring with the tractor man from the village — I pay him, I have no tractor. Then I plant after the Qingming festival, when the ground is warm enough.

I water from my well. First water after planting so the seeds come up. Then when it flowers, then when bolls are forming. Three, maybe four times if the summer is dry. Water is not free — the pump uses electricity.

The spraying — cotton is a lot of work for spraying. The aphids come, the red spider comes, the bollworm comes even with the new seed. I spray many times, maybe 8 or 9 times through the summer. I carry the sprayer on my back. My back hurts now but I still do it.

If the year is good, I get maybe 250 jin of cotton each mu. That is what I usually get. 2 mu, so about 500 jin total. Not much, but enough for us.
